blurb: Guests explore Edisto Island's natural and cultural history through boat ecotours focusing on dolphins, the ACE Basin estuary, and African American history. Walking tours include beachcombing to learn about shells, fossils, and local animals. Cooking lessons offer hands-on experience with Sea Island cooking in the Gullah tradition.

quotes.text: Our extended family of 14 enjoyed an amazing meal with Marvetta Hutchinson!! Don't miss the chance to meet her, learn about Gullah culture, and have a delicious meal! We go to Edisto every year and are adding "Cooking with Marvetta" to the list of annual traditions. Thanks Captain Meg and Marvetta for a wonderful experience.

Meg was pleasant, informative, very knowledgeable. The boat was comfortable and well suited to touring. The information about the marina, how long the walk was very helpful. We were able to take one of our party that is severely mobility limited and made it work.

Loved our beach walk with Catherine she was so informative. Usually you go to the beach pick up a few shells swim in the ocean. We got great context on our beach, sea turtles,area history. I can’t recommend this more

We had a great time on the tour and it's definitely a must do on Edisto Island. The biodiversity on the island is incredible and absolutely worth seeing from the water. Definitely a dog friendly activity!
